value.body: A dietitian plans diets for people with medical conditions and for healthy groups. Hospitals, clinics, diabetes and kidney-care centres, food-service companies and wellness firms hire dietitians. A typical day involves assessing patients, planning therapeutic diets with doctors, counselling patients and families, and checking hospital meals.

items.label: Typical entry
items.value: B.Sc Nutrition & Dietetics or Home Science (Food & Nutrition); many add an M.Sc or PG diploma

items.label: Professional credential
items.note: Indian Dietetic Association exam after a degree, a PG qualification and a supervised internship (as reported)

items.label: Common workplaces
items.value: Hospitals, clinics, food service, wellness firms

value.title: How you get in
value.body: A B.Sc in nutrition, dietetics or home science (food and nutrition), usually followed by an M.Sc or PG diploma in dietetics and a hospital internship. Freshers often start as trainee or assistant dietitians. Many hospital posts prefer or require the RD credential.

value.title: At a glance
items: Clinical posts usually expect a postgraduate qualification or internship, not only a B.Sc.
Next roles: senior or chief dietitian, clinical nutrition lead, diabetes educator, or private practice.
Government dietitian posts (railways, central and state hospitals) are few and notified irregularly.
